name: KamLAND detector

experiment_ids.note: KamLAND-Zen suspends a xenon-loaded inner balloon 'at the center of the KamLAND detector' (arXiv:1211.3863); it does not have its own separate detector: record (owned by the neutrino-mass-0vbb workstream, which references this detector:kamland id directly per ID_REGISTRY).

technology.value: Liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector: 1 kton of liquid scintillator in a 13-m-diameter spherical balloon, with an oil buffer between the balloon and an 18-m-diameter spherical stainless-steel containment vessel lined with 1,879 photomultiplier tubes, surrounded by a 3.2 kton water-Cherenkov outer detector that tags cosmic-ray muons
technology.quote: 1 kton of ultra-pure LS contained in a 13-m-diameter spherical balloon ... between the balloon and an 18-m-diameter spherical stainless-steel containment vessel ... The containment vessel is surrounded by a 3.2 kton water-Cherenkov detector
technology.note: Configuration as described in the KamLAND first-results paper (arXiv:hep-ex/0212021, Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 021802): 13 m balloon, 18 m containment vessel, 1,879 PMTs, 3.2 kton water-Cherenkov outer detector. CORRECTED: the previous value called the 18 m sphere the scintillator balloon; the balloon is 13 m and the 18 m sphere is the stainless-steel containment vessel. This record is referenced by the neutrino-mass-0vbb workstream for KamLAND-Zen (which reuses this same detector volume with a different central balloon/isotope load); the placement/site below is the load-bearing fact for that reference and is sourced accordingly.

summary.plain: A giant balloon of clear liquid inside a mine in Japan, watched by nearly 1,900 light sensors, that catches antineutrinos from nuclear reactors across the country. A xenon-loaded inner balloon suspended at its centre (KamLAND-Zen) uses the same detector to search for a different rare process.
summary.technical: ~1000 t liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector in an 18 m diameter vessel with 1,879 PMTs, surrounded by a water-Cherenkov muon veto, in the old Kamiokande cavity of the Kamioka mine; operating since 2002-01-17.
